VERDICT: CLEAN
BOUNDARY: The proof assumes \(x<y\), so the interval is nondegenerate; degenerate intervals do not support differentiability.  The endpoint case (\(\lambda=f'(x)\) or \(\lambda=f'(y)\)) is explicit.  In the strict case, step 2.1 uses the derivative inequalities to obtain \(h(x+s)<h(x)\) and \(h(y-t)<h(y)\), which forces the minimum of \(h\) on \([x,y]\) to lie in \((x,y)\).  Hence the extremum is interior to \(I\) and Fermat applies.  No counterexample to the theorem or to the proof’s logic was found.
